turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Well, what brings me in is... I just can't seem to get past how rough and worn my face and hands look lately. 

It feels like every time I have to go into town, every banker or county person is just staring right at all the cracks, the sun spots, and the sagging skin. My wife tells me I'm making too much of it, she says I just look like a normal man who's worked outdoors for a living. But I just can't stop focusing on it. It's really starting to bother me.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes an inability to stop focusing on perceived flaws in his skin, face, and hands (cracks, sun spots, sagging), which his wife considers normal for someone working outdoors.

turns.doctor_question: If other people were not able to see your face or hands, would this still bother you as much?
turns.patient_response: I... I don't really know. I haven't really thought about it like that before. I mean, I guess I just always assume everyone can see it, you know? So I'm not sure if it would bother me as much if they couldn't. It's hard to say.

turns.doctor_question: Are you afraid that people will judge you negatively because of how your face and hands look?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure. I haven't really thought about whether they're... judging me, exactly. I mean, I don't know what's going through their heads. I just know they're looking right at the rough spots and the sagging skin. But as far as being afraid that they think less of me or something... I couldn't really say.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself repeatedly checking your face or hands in mirrors or other reflective surfaces?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I do. Especially before I have to leave for a loan meeting, or... or if we're setting up a table at a craft fair. I'll keep checking the bathroom mirror, and then I'll check the mirror on my truck, too. 

I just stand there, turning my hat this way and that, trying to see how it looks. And I catch myself looking at my hands and comparing them to the younger workers' hands. I do it so much that... well, I end up wasting a good bit of time that I really should be using to actually work on the farm.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient explicitly confirms repeatedly checking bathroom and truck mirrors and comparing his hands to younger workers' hands, resulting in significant time wasted.

turns.doctor_question: Have you started avoiding going into town, meetings, or fairs because you feel embarrassed about how your face or hands look?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, it's gotten to that point. I've actually missed a few important calls with bankers recently, and... well, I've put off some big decisions for the farm. I just couldn't get myself looking acceptable enough to sit down with people, even over a video call. And my wife's been trying to get some new photos of us to promote the retreat and our craft sales, but I've just stopped agreeing to do them. I can't stand the thought of those pictures being out there for everyone to see.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient confirms avoiding meetings, calls, and photographs due to intense distress over their appearance and being unable to make themselves look acceptable.

turns.doctor_question: Has anyone besides your wife told you that the problems you see in your face or hands are only slight or not really noticeable?
turns.patient_response: No, I can't say they have. But... well, I don't exactly talk about this with anyone else. It's not really something I'd bring up with the guys helping out on the farm, or the folks at the bank. So, no, nobody besides my wife has said anything about it one way or the other.

turns.doctor_question: Do unwanted thoughts about how your face or hands look keep popping into your mind even when you try not to think about them?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I think about it when I'm looking in the mirror or when I have to go see people, like I said. But if I'm just out working in the field or fixing a tractor, my mind is usually on the work. I don't just have thoughts about it pop up out of nowhere when I'm busy doing other things.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient explicitly denies having intrusive, unwanted thoughts popping into their mind out of nowhere when engaged in other activities.

turns.doctor_question: Do you believe your face and hands look abnormal or defective, even though your wife says they look normal for someone who has worked outdoors?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, I really do. Like I was just saying, that's the whole reason I finally came in to see you. I know she says I just look like a man who's worked outdoors his whole life, but... I just can't get past how rough and worn they are. 

To me, it's not just normal aging. The sagging skin, the spots, the deep cracks... it feels wrong. Defective, I guess you could say. turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

It bothers me a lot when I have to go into town or deal with folks. But overall... no, my mood is mostly fine. I still get up and get my work done every day without feeling down about life in general.

turns.patient_response: No, I don't think I would. If I didn't have to worry about people staring at my skin and all these spots and cracks, I'd be fine. I've never had a problem talking to the bank folks or getting my picture taken before this started bothering me so much. It's really just... it's just about how I look. If that was fixed, the anxiety about those meetings would be gone.
